requirements.quote:
Newer
   clients or servers, when communicating with newer peers, should
   negotiate the most preferred common parameters.
requirements.condition: a newer client communicates with a newer peer
requirements.required_behavior: negotiate the most preferred parameters common to both peers
requirements.why_checkable: Client negotiation tests can compare the selected parameters with both peers' supported sets and preference ordering.

requirements.quote:
Newer
   clients or servers, when communicating with newer peers, should
   negotiate the most preferred common parameters.
requirements.condition: a newer server communicates with a newer peer
requirements.required_behavior: negotiate the most preferred parameters common to both peers
requirements.why_checkable: Server negotiation tests can compare the selected parameters with both peers' supported sets and preference ordering.

requirements.quote:
The TLS handshake
   provides downgrade protection: Middleboxes passing traffic between a
   newer client and newer server without terminating TLS should be
   unable to influence the handshake (see Appendix E.1).
requirements.condition: a middlebox passes traffic between a newer client and a newer server without terminating TLS
requirements.required_behavior: preserve the end-to-end handshake so that the middlebox cannot influence it
requirements.forbidden_behavior: allow the non-terminating middlebox to influence the handshake
requirements.why_checkable: Active-middlebox tests can attempt to alter negotiation and verify that endpoint handshake integrity prevents influence.

requirements.quote:
A client sending a ClientHello MUST support all parameters
       advertised in it.
requirements.required_behavior: support every parameter advertised in the ClientHello
requirements.forbidden_behavior: advertise a parameter the client does not support
requirements.why_checkable: The ClientHello builder and capability state can be inspected or tested for advertisement-support consistency.

requirements.quote:
A server receiving a ClientHello MUST correctly ignore all
       unrecognized cipher suites, extensions, and other parameters.
requirements.condition: a server receives a ClientHello containing an unrecognized cipher suite
requirements.why_checkable: A parser test can inject an unknown cipher-suite value and observe that it is ignored.

requirements.quote:
A server receiving a ClientHello MUST correctly ignore all
       unrecognized cipher suites, extensions, and other parameters.
requirements.condition: a server receives a ClientHello containing an unrecognized extension
requirements.why_checkable: A parser test can inject an unknown extension type and observe that it is ignored.

requirements.quote:
A server receiving a ClientHello MUST correctly ignore all
       unrecognized cipher suites, extensions, and other parameters.
requirements.condition: a server receives a ClientHello containing another unrecognized parameter
requirements.why_checkable: A message-decoding test can supply an otherwise valid unknown parameter and observe that it is ignored.

requirements.quote:
In
       TLS 1.3, a client receiving a CertificateRequest or
       NewSessionTicket MUST also ignore all unrecognized extensions.
requirements.condition: a TLS 1.3 client receives a CertificateRequest containing an unrecognized extension
requirements.why_checkable: A CertificateRequest parsing test can include an unknown extension and verify that client processing continues without acting on it.

requirements.quote:
In
       TLS 1.3, a client receiving a CertificateRequest or
       NewSessionTicket MUST also ignore all unrecognized extensions.
requirements.condition: a TLS 1.3 client receives a NewSessionTicket containing an unrecognized extension
requirements.why_checkable: A NewSessionTicket parsing test can include an unknown extension and verify that client processing continues without acting on it.

requirements.quote:
A middlebox which terminates a TLS connection MUST behave as a
       compliant TLS server (to the original client), including having a
       certificate which the client is willing to accept, and also as a
       compliant TLS client (to the original server), including verifying
       the original server's certificate.
requirements.condition: a middlebox terminates the original client's TLS connection
requirements.required_behavior: behave as a compliant TLS server toward the original client
requirements.why_checkable: The client-facing leg can be exercised with TLS server conformance tests.

requirements.quote:
A middlebox which terminates a TLS connection MUST behave as a
       compliant TLS server (to the original client), including having a
       certificate which the client is willing to accept, and also as a
       compliant TLS client (to the original server), including verifying
       the original server's certificate.
requirements.condition: a middlebox acts as a terminating TLS server toward the original client
requirements.required_behavior: present a certificate that the original client is willing to accept
requirements.why_checkable: A client-facing handshake test can validate the middlebox certificate against the client's acceptance policy.

requirements.quote:
A middlebox which terminates a TLS connection MUST behave as a
       compliant TLS server (to the original client), including having a
       certificate which the client is willing to accept, and also as a
       compliant TLS client (to the original server), including verifying
       the original server's certificate.
requirements.condition: a middlebox terminates a TLS connection and connects to the original server
requirements.required_behavior: behave as a compliant TLS client toward the original server
requirements.why_checkable: The server-facing leg can be exercised with TLS client conformance tests.

requirements.quote:
A middlebox which terminates a TLS connection MUST behave as a
       compliant TLS server (to the original client), including having a
       certificate which the client is willing to accept, and also as a
       compliant TLS client (to the original server), including verifying
       the original server's certificate.
requirements.condition: a terminating middlebox connects as a TLS client to the original server
requirements.why_checkable: Server-certificate validation tests can supply valid and invalid chains and observe the middlebox decision.

requirements.quote:
In particular, it MUST
       generate its own ClientHello containing only parameters it
       understands, and it MUST generate a fresh ServerHello random
       value, rather than forwarding the endpoint's value.
requirements.condition: a middlebox terminates a TLS connection and initiates the server-facing handshake
requirements.forbidden_behavior: forward the original endpoint's ClientHello in place of generating its own
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake capture can distinguish a middlebox-generated ClientHello from a forwarded endpoint message.

requirements.quote:
In particular, it MUST
       generate its own ClientHello containing only parameters it
       understands, and it MUST generate a fresh ServerHello random
       value, rather than forwarding the endpoint's value.
requirements.condition: a terminating middlebox generates its own ClientHello
requirements.required_behavior: include only parameters the middlebox understands
requirements.forbidden_behavior: include a parameter the middlebox does not understand
requirements.why_checkable: Generated ClientHello contents can be compared with the middlebox's implemented parameter set.

requirements.quote:
In particular, it MUST
       generate its own ClientHello containing only parameters it
       understands, and it MUST generate a fresh ServerHello random
       value, rather than forwarding the endpoint's value.
requirements.condition: a terminating middlebox generates a ServerHello toward the original client
requirements.required_behavior: generate a fresh ServerHello random value
requirements.forbidden_behavior: forward the original server endpoint's ServerHello random value
requirements.why_checkable: Captured client-facing and server-facing ServerHello messages can be checked for independently generated random values.

requirements.quote:
A middlebox which forwards ClientHello parameters it does not
       understand MUST NOT process any messages beyond that ClientHello.
requirements.condition: a middlebox forwards ClientHello parameters it does not understand
requirements.forbidden_behavior: process any message after that ClientHello
requirements.why_checkable: A traffic test can use an unknown forwarded parameter and detect any subsequent message parsing or transformation.

requirements.quote: It MUST forward all subsequent traffic unmodified.
requirements.condition: a middlebox has forwarded ClientHello parameters it does not understand
requirements.required_behavior: forward all traffic after that ClientHello without modification
requirements.why_checkable: Byte-for-byte comparison across both sides of the middlebox can verify that all subsequent traffic is forwarded unchanged.
